definitions.explanation: Metal money as opposed to paper money.

examples.japanese: {自動|じどう}{販売|はんばい}{機|き}に{硬貨|こうか}を{入|い}れた。
examples.english: I put coins into the vending machine.

examples.japanese: 500{円|えん}{硬貨|こうか}は{重|おも}い。
{財布|さいふ}に{硬貨|こうか}がたくさんある。
examples.english: I have a lot of coins in my wallet.

notes:
{硬貨|こうか} refers to metal coins.

JAPANESE COINS:
- 1{円|えん}{硬貨|こうか} (1-yen coin - aluminum)
- 5{円|えん}{硬貨|こうか} (5-yen coin - brass, has a hole)
- 10{円|えん}{硬貨|こうか} (10-yen coin - bronze)
- 50{円|えん}{硬貨|こうか} (50-yen coin - cupronickel, has a hole)
- 100{円|えん}{硬貨|こうか} (100-yen coin - cupronickel)
- 500{円|えん}{硬貨|こうか} (500-yen coin - nickel-brass)

CONTRAST:
- {硬貨|こうか} (coins) ↔ {紙幣|しへい}/{札|さつ} (paper money, bills)

RELATED:
- {小銭|こぜに} (coins, small change - casual term)
